Item [4] ('should: Move stable test review design context…') is the only 'should'; all others are 'must' — but there is no 'nice-to-have' tier considered, and the impactOnExisting list (4 items) has no priority labels at all. (at scopeVerification.in); Prioritize Requirements — impactOnExisting — 4 items with no priority labels — The four impact items represent work that consumers of changed modules must perform, but none is labeled must/should/nice-to-have, making it impossible to determine what is required versus optional for the spec to be considered complete. (at scopeVerification.in[1]); Proactively Raise Related Implications — missing implication: systemPrompt passed to Agent.call may count toward context window differently per provider, affecting cost estimates — Moving stable instructions to the system prompt changes token distribution between system and user roles, which can affect cost-per-call calculations. entries.reason: Single Responsibility — The spec addresses one concern: restoring prompt-cache creation for review prompts via PromptBuilder refactoring and adding provider/profile attribution to flow metrics. All sub-items are causally linked to that concern.; Unambiguous Requirements — "move reviewer role text, focus/rule bullets, and output-format instructions into system prompts" — 'focus/rule bullets' is vague — it does not specify which bullets or sections qualify as non-varying, making it ambiguous what content must move to the system side. (at goal); Unambiguous Requirements — "instructions that do not vary per call are not separated into the provider system prompt path" — 'Instructions that do not vary per call' is a subjective criterion without an enumerated list; two reviewers might disagree on which instructions are invariant. (at analysis.problem); Unambiguous Requirements — "enrich agent metric entries with provider/profile metadata" — 'Enrich' is vague; the requirement does not state which specific fields must be added or the exact key names, making it unverifiable without reading downstream requirements. (at analysis.proposedApproach); Unambiguous Requirements — "providers that charge system tokens at full rate or do not cache them" — No verifiable condition is stated for how cost must be reported when a provider does not cache system tokens — 'can increase per-call cost' is observational, not a testable requirement. (at analysis.proposedApproach); Unambiguous Requirements — "Move the single `testDesign` value created before `runReviewLoop` to the systemPrompt argument" — 'Move to the systemPrompt argument' for a 'should' item without a verifiable acceptance condition (e.g., cacheCreation > 0 or unit test assertion) makes it untestable as stated. (at scopeVerification.in[4] (should item)); Complete Context — "review prompt builders call agents with a non-empty systemPrompt containing reviewer role/focus/output-format text" — 'Non-empty systemPrompt containing reviewer role/focus/output-format text' is insufficiently specific — two reviewers would not agree on what exact content satisfies 'reviewer role/focus/output-format text' without a concrete example or schema. (at scopeVerification.in[8] (test assertion list)); Complete Context — "aggregate cost equals the exact sum of input costs" — 'Input costs' is ambiguous: it is unclear whether this means only input tokens, all token types, or a named cost field; the phrasing conflicts with the broader 'cost totals' language used elsewhere. (at scopeVerification.in[8] (test assertion list)); Complete Context — "provider buckets use `provider:profileKey`" — The format of the compound key is stated but the allowed character set, separator escaping rules, and behavior when provider or profileKey contains a colon are not specified. (at scopeVerification.in[8] (test assertion list)); Complete Context — "metric entries include provider/profile fields" — 'Provider/profile fields' is not defined with specific key names or value constraints here, so it is unclear when an implementation satisfies this requirement independent of the scopeVerification list. (at impactOnExisting[3]); No Hardcoded Secrets — The spec contains no API keys, passwords, tokens, or other secrets.; Prioritize Requirements — impactOnExisting list (6 items, mix of must/should without explicit priority labels on items 4–6) — The impactOnExisting section contains more than three items; items 4–6 carry implicit 'must' labels but two items ('should') are not assigned an explicit must/should/nice-to-have priority tag, making the priority scheme incomplete for a section treated as requirements. (at impactOnExisting); Prioritize Requirements — "should: `sdd-forge flow get status` JSON metricsSummary … should expose provider/profile buckets" — The 'should' label is used here as a priority label, but the prioritize-requirements article requires explicit must/should/nice-to-have classification; 'should' as used here conflates RFC-style language with priority tier, making it ambiguous whether this is a SHOULD-level requirement or a nice-to-have. (at impactOnExisting[5]); Impact on Existing Features — The spec explicitly enumerates affected existing features in the impactOnExisting section, covering PromptBuilder consumers, review commands, docs commands, agent/provider/flow-store metric paths, token command, get-status, and existing tests.; Present Recommendations with Reasoning — Each qa entry states a recommended answer, cites evidence (file paths, specific functions, or Issue references), explains the reasoning, and records rejected alternatives under 'considered'.; Explore Before Asking — All qa entries reference concrete evidence from the codebase (specific file paths and function names), indicating exploration was performed before answering. openQuestions is empty.; Proactively Raise Related Implications — Moving text from user prompt to system prompt can increase per-call cost for providers that charge system tokens at full rate — The cost-increase implication is mentioned in a single parenthetical but is not elevated into a named risk item with a mitigation or decision — a downstream reviewer could overlook it, and no explicit requirement tracks cost regression detection beyond a test assertion. (at analysis.proposedApproach); Proactively Raise Related Implications — Docs command migrations should preserve current user-prompt-only behavior unless the call site already passes a systemPrompt — The implication that docs commands currently never split system/user prompts and could accidentally start sending a system prompt if the migration pattern is applied incorrectly is not raised as a risk; no requirement guards against introducing an inadvertent system prompt in docs pipelines. (at scopeVerification.in[2] and qa[2]); Confirm Brainstorm vs. Decision Before Critiquing — The spec is a decided design (approval.approved=true); no unchecked brainstorming items remain in openQuestions or in the qa section.; Capture Digressions in draft.md — No digressions are evident; openQuestions is empty and all discussed alternatives are captured in each qa entry's 'considered' field.; Backward-Compatible CLI Interface — The spec explicitly excludes changing public CLI command names or options in scopeVerification.out, and the PromptBuilder API change is internal/library-level with no public CLI surface affected.
